environment.description: Equivalent local developer reference environment; in-process ASGI client boundary with a local Docker PostgreSQL pool

protocol.clock_boundary: committed enqueue_compute acknowledgement to the ASGI send carrying the first persisted run_progress frame
protocol.clock_boundary_note: Story 3.6 has not shipped the HTTP creation command, so the direct transaction commit is the acknowledgement boundary. Delivery is observed at ASGI send; network transit is excluded. SCOPE LIMIT: run.queued.v1 is written by create_queued_run INSIDE the enqueue transaction, and the stream is opened only after that transaction commits, so the measured path contains no queue, no worker, no solver and no lock contention -- it is an HTTP connect plus one indexed row read, and cannot exceed the threshold by construction. These figures bound read-path delivery latency; they do NOT measure queue-to-visible latency. The wait a planner actually experiences is gated by worker lease acquisition and is first observable at run.running.v1, which this story does not measure. Owner: Story 3.11 (worker kill / lease expiry).

version_bindings.dataset: 2 governed fixtures (sample_tiny_input:v1, sample_tiny_input_more_tm:v1); contract sha256 digests recorded alongside
version_bindings.tool: direct committed enqueue_compute bundle plus in-process ASGI driver over the real FastAPI app and PostgreSQL 18 in Docker Desktop
version_bindings.policy: NFR35/AD-26: the first persisted schedule-run event reaches the connected client within 5000 ms; every measured run must pass
version_bindings.solver: not applicable — the queued event precedes solver execution
